findings.quote: but sought to raise only one or two, and hardly even those,
findings.problem: ἀλλὰ μόλις ἓν τῶν πλείστων ἢ δύο ... θρέψαι: μόλις means 'at most / barely' one or two (out of the many born). It does not mean they 'hardly' raised even those one or two. The added restriction misreads μόλις.
findings.proposed_fix: but raised at most one or two of the many born,

findings.quote: released from great internal strife and civil slaughter through Roman favor.
findings.problem: The Greek breaks off here: διὰ τῆς Ῥωμαίων... φιλοτ̣ιμίας:... followed by a fragmentary clause (ἅμα δυσμενείας μὲν ἢ βλάβης τῆς ἐν τοῖς πρότερον καιροῖς πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ...). The English closes the sentence with no gap marked before the next fragment.
findings.proposed_fix: released from great internal strife and civil slaughter through Roman generosity [...] [fragmentary text follows] [...]

findings.quote: whereas in the earlier days, under the kings who were truly kings, they had already experienced [...]
findings.problem: πλείστους ... φυγαδευθέντας καὶ στρεβλωθέντας καὶ φονευθέντας ἢ τῶν ἐν τοῖς πρότερον καιροῖς ὑπὸ τῶν κατ᾽ ἀλήθειαν βασι[λέων]: ἢ is comparative. They saw more of their people exiled, tortured and killed in a short time than under the true kings in earlier times. 'whereas ... they had already experienced' turns the comparison into a contrast, and the clause is built from fragmentary words (ἤδη τοῦτο γε ε̣χ̣...) that belong to the lacuna.
findings.proposed_fix: more than in earlier times under the true kings [...]

findings.quote: they were angered at the Roman encampment itself and regretted their former wrongs against themselves [...] [fragmentary text continues].
findings.problem: The Greek reads only ...Ῥωμαίων στρατοπεδεύματος ἐξ αὐτῆς μεταμέλοι: ἐν ἀδικ... τῶν πρὸ τοῦ Ψευδοφιλίππου μὲν εἰς αὐτοὺς παρανομημάτων. There is no 'angered'. The παρανομήματα are lawless acts committed against them (εἰς αὐτούς) before the Pseudo-Philip, not 'their' wrongs. The English also leaves out the legible sentence after the gap: ... πολλῶν τε μετὰ μὲν τοῦ Δημητρίου καὶ πάλιν μετὰ Περσέως μαχόμενοι πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἡττήθησαν, ἀνδρὶ δὲ στυγνῷ συναγωνιζόμενοι καὶ περὶ τῆς τούτου βασιλείας ἀνδραγαθήσαντες ἐνίκησαν Ῥωμαίους. This μὲν ... δέ contrast is the puzzle that the next sentence ('who would not be puzzled') refers to. The MS has Δημητρίου, kept as transmitted (historically one expects Philip V); the name is not emended here.
findings.proposed_fix: [...] the Roman camp [...] regret [...] the lawless acts committed against them before the Pseudo-Philip [...]. [...] And though they had fought against the Romans with Demetrius, and again with Perseus, and been defeated, yet fighting alongside a hateful man and showing courage in defense of his kingship, they defeated the Romans.

units.note: The Macedonian section (from διὰ τῆς Ῥωμαίων onward) is badly lacunose in the Greek. The fixes only mark the gaps and drop connective sense the English invented; they do not restore the text. 'Demetrius' is as transmitted and may be an error for Philip; it is left unresolved.
